intro.title: How it works
intro.body: The AS/400 Collector is a Linux service that connects directly to your AS/400 (IBM i) systems and pulls security journal entries, then streams them securely to UTMStack for correlation and alerting.
intro.note: Nothing is installed on the AS/400 itself — the Collector runs on a Linux host that has network access to your AS/400 systems.

intro.body: Sophos Central provides secure APIs to retrieve event and alert data. UTMStack connects to those APIs to centralize monitoring and enhance your security visibility — no agent or forwarder required.

sophos.apiSection: Generate API Credentials in Sophos Central

apiCredentials.title: Open API Credentials Management
apiCredentials.body: In <hl>Sophos Central Admin</hl>, navigate to <hl>Global Settings → API Credentials Management</hl>.

addCredential.title: Create a new credential

copyIds.title: Copy Client ID and Client Secret
copyIds.body: Copy the <hl>Client ID</hl> and <hl>Client Secret</hl> and store them securely.
copyIds.secretNote: The Client Secret is shown only once. Save it somewhere safe before closing this dialog.

credentials.title: Add Sophos Central credentials
credentials.body: Enter the credentials you just created. You can add more than one Sophos account by clicking Add tenant.

apiAccess.title: 3 · Open API Access
apiAccess.body: From the Subscriptions tab, click on the API Access tab.

createCredential.title: 4 · Create a client credential
createCredential.body: Click New and fill in the Name and Description. Read the SecureAnywhere Business Solution and Unity API agreement, then click Create.

noteClientSecret.title: 5 · Copy the client ID and secret
noteClientSecret.body: Save the Client ID from the list and the Client Secret that's shown only once. Click "I have made note of the client secret" to confirm.

fillForm.title: 6 · Fill the form
fillForm.body: Provide the client ID and client secret to UTMStack. You can add more than one Webroot tenant if needed.

activate.title: 7 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so Webroot events start flowing.

syslog.title: Configure the Syslog integration
syslog.body: Go to <hl>Integrations → Syslog</hl> and enable it. Set the host to <hl>{{host}}</hl> and port to <hl>{{port}}</hl>, keep the format as <hl>CEF</hl>, click <hl>Test</hl> to verify the connection, then <hl>Save</hl>.

intro.title: How it works

azurePortal.title: Open Microsoft Entra ID

appRegistrations.title: Go to App registrations
appRegistrations.body: In the left menu, click <hl>App registrations</hl>.

registerApp.title: Register a new app

clientSecret.title: Create a client secret
clientSecret.body: Go to <hl>Certificates & Secrets → New client secret</hl>. Add a description, set expiry to <hl>730 days (24 months)</hl>, and click <hl>Add</hl>.

activityFeed.title: Grant ActivityFeed permissions
activityFeed.body: Select <hl>Application Permissions</hl> and add <hl>ActivityFeed.Read</hl> and <hl>ActivityFeed.ReadDlp</hl>. Click <hl>Grant admin consent</hl> and confirm.

graphPermissions.title: Add Microsoft Graph permissions
graphPermissions.body: Back in <hl>Add a permission</hl>, click <hl>Microsoft Graph</hl>.

delegatedPermissions.title: Add delegated SecurityAlert permissions
delegatedPermissions.body: Select <hl>Delegated Permissions</hl> and add <hl>SecurityAlert.Read.All</hl> and <hl>SecurityAlert.ReadWrite.All</hl>. Click <hl>Grant admin consent</hl> and confirm.

appPermissions.title: Add application SecurityAlert permissions
appPermissions.body: Select <hl>Application Permissions</hl> and add <hl>SecurityAlert.Read.All</hl> and <hl>SecurityAlert.ReadWrite.All</hl>. Click <hl>Grant admin consent</hl> and confirm.

noteIds.title: Copy the app IDs

credentials.title: Connect your Microsoft 365 tenant

save.title: 6 · Save

copyCredentials.title: 8 · Copy the consumer key and secret
copyCredentials.body: Verify your identity. The Consumer Key and Consumer Secret appear under "Consumer Details". Copy both with the Copy button.

fillForm.title: 9 · Fill the form
fillForm.body: Provide the Consumer Key, Consumer Secret, Salesforce username and password to UTMStack.

activate.title: 10 · Activate

addRoles.title: 2 · Add Roles and Features

selectCertServices.title: 3 · Select Active Directory Certificate Services
selectCertServices.body: On the Server Roles step, select Active Directory Certificate Services.

installServices.title: 4 · Install the Certificate Authority role service

configureAdCs.title: 5 · Configure AD CS

pickCaType.title: 6 · Pick the CA type

setValidity.title: 7 · Set the certificate validity period
setValidity.body: Set a validity period that fits your organization (5 years is typical).

confirm.title: 8 · Confirm and install

activate.title: 10 · Activate

chooseProvider.title: 2 · Choose a provider

configureCredentials.title: 3 · Configure credentials

intro.title: How it works
intro.body: UTMStack reads audit activity directly from Google Cloud via Pub/Sub. A Logs Router sink streams your project logs into a Pub/Sub topic; UTMStack runs an internal puller that reads a Pull subscription on that topic using a service-account key. Nothing is installed in your GCP project.
intro.note: No agent runs in GCP — UTMStack pulls messages from the Pub/Sub subscription using the service-account JSON key you provide below.

createTopic.title: Create a Pub/Sub topic
createTopic.body: In the Google Cloud console, open Pub/Sub → Topics and create a new topic. The Logs Router sink will publish your project logs to it.

createSubscription.title: Create a subscription
createSubscription.body: From the topic menu, create a subscription. UTMStack pulls messages from this subscription.

configureSubscription.title: Configure the subscription
configureSubscription.body: Leave the Delivery type as Pull and the Expiration as Never expire. The default acknowledgement deadline (10s) and message retention are fine.

logsRouter.title: Open Logs Router and create a sink
logsRouter.body: Navigate to Logging → Logs Router and create a new sink. This is what forwards your project logs into the Pub/Sub topic above.

sinkDestination.title: Point the sink at the topic
sinkDestination.body: Choose Cloud Pub/Sub topic as the sink destination and select the topic you created. Optionally use inclusion/exclusion filters to scope which logs are forwarded, then create the sink.

serviceAccount.title: Create a service account
serviceAccount.body: Open IAM & Admin → Service Accounts in the project that holds your topic and sink, and create a new service account. Grant it the Pub/Sub Editor role so UTMStack can pull from the subscription.

serviceAccountKey.title: Generate a key for the service account
serviceAccountKey.body: Open the service account, go to the Keys tab, and add a new key. Choose JSON as the key type.

downloadKey.title: Download the JSON key
downloadKey.body: Save the JSON file Google downloads — its contents go in the Service account JSON key field below. The key is shown only once.

credentials.title: Pub/Sub configuration
credentials.body: Use the values collected above to configure UTMStack. You can monitor more than one project by saving additional configurations.

mapping.projectId: Project ID — the GCP project that holds your topic, subscription and sink
mapping.subscription: Subscription name — the Pull subscription created in step 2
mapping.jsonKey: Service account JSON key — the file downloaded in step 8

intro.title: How it works
intro.body: UTMStack reads audit activity directly from an Azure Event Hub. You configure your Azure subscription to stream events into an Event Hub; UTMStack runs an internal puller that reads that hub and checkpoints its progress in a Storage Account. Nothing is installed in your Azure tenant.
intro.note: No agent runs in Azure — UTMStack pulls events from the Event Hub using the connection strings you provide below.

createEventHub.title: Create an Event Hub
createEventHub.body: In the Azure Portal, create an Event Hubs namespace and an Event Hub inside it. UTMStack will read events from this hub.
createEventHub.docLabel: Quickstart: Create an event hub using the Azure portal

sharedAccessPolicy.title: Add a Shared Access Policy
sharedAccessPolicy.body: Open the Event Hub → Shared access policies and create a new policy. Make sure you select the Listen permission.

connectionString.title: Copy the primary connection string
connectionString.body: Open the Shared access policy you just created and copy the Connection string–primary key. You will use it to configure your tenant below.

consumerGroup.title: Create a dedicated consumer group
consumerGroup.body: Get the Consumer Group name in: All services → Event Hubs → your namespace → Event Hubs → your instance → Consumer groups. You will use it to configure your tenant below.
consumerGroup.warn: Create a consumer group specifically for UTMStack. Do not use $Default or any other group already in use — reusing a consumer group across unrelated consumers can cause unexpected behavior and lost events. All UTMStack instances should share the same consumer group so they can process events together.

createStorageAccount.title: Create a Storage Account
createStorageAccount.body: UTMStack needs a Storage Account to checkpoint its read position. Create one in the same region as the Event Hub.

storageContainer.title: Get the Storage Container name
storageContainer.body: Get the Storage Container name in: All services → Storage accounts → your account → Containers. You will use it to configure your tenant below.

storageConnection.title: Copy the Storage Account connection string
storageConnection.body: Get the Storage Account connection string with key in: All services → Storage accounts → your account → Access keys. UTMStack uses it to store Event Hub checkpoints.

eventGrid.title: Register the Event Grid resource provider
eventGrid.body: Configure your subscription to send logs to the Event Hub. Go to Subscriptions → Resource providers, search for Event Grid (Microsoft.EventGrid) and make sure it is registered.

createEventSubscription.title: Create an Event Subscription
createEventSubscription.body: In the subscription Events panel, create a new event by clicking Events → Event Subscription.

configureEventSubscription.title: Point the Event Subscription at your Event Hub
configureEventSubscription.body: Configure the Event Subscription to send logs to the Event Hub you created in step 1.

credentials.title: Event Hub configuration
credentials.body: Use the data collected in the steps above to configure UTMStack. You can add more than one Event Hub by saving additional configurations.

mapping.consumerGroup: Consumer group — value obtained in step 4

intro.title: How it works
intro.body: UTMStack reads audit activity directly from AWS CloudWatch Logs. CloudTrail captures API calls and management events across your AWS account, forwards them to a CloudWatch log group, and UTMStack polls that group to ingest and correlate events.
intro.note: No agent is installed on AWS — UTMStack pulls log events using read-only IAM credentials you provide below.

dashboard.title: Open the IAM dashboard
dashboard.body: Open the AWS console, navigate to the IAM dashboard and select Users.

addUser.title: Add a user
addUser.body: Click Add user, enter a descriptive user name, and proceed to the next step.

attachPolicy.title: Attach the read-only policy
attachPolicy.body: Under Permissions, attach the required policy. Select CloudWatchLogsReadOnlyAccess for read-only CloudWatch access.

createUser.title: Create the user
createUser.body: Review the configuration and click Create user to provision the account.

openUser.title: Open the new user
openUser.body: Open the newly created user by clicking its name to view details and manage credentials.

securityTab.title: Go to Security credentials
securityTab.body: Select the Security credentials tab to create programmatic access keys.

createKey.title: Create an access key
createKey.body: Click Create access key and choose the option for an application running outside AWS (programmatic access).

confirmKey.title: Confirm creation
confirmKey.body: Confirm creation of the access key. AWS will generate an Access Key ID and Secret Access Key.

downloadKey.title: Save your credentials
downloadKey.body: Download the credentials file or copy the Access Key ID and Secret Access Key to a secure location — the Secret Access Key is only shown once.

credentials.title: Enter credentials
credentials.body: Paste the Access Key ID and Secret Access Key obtained in the previous steps. UTMStack verifies the credentials against AWS before saving.

createGroup.title: Create a CloudWatch Log Group
createGroup.body: Open the CloudWatch console, choose Log management and click Create log group.

nameGroup.title: Name the log group and set retention
nameGroup.body: Enter the log group name utmstack and set retention to 1 day. Click Create log group.

openTrail.title: Open CloudTrail and create a trail
openTrail.body: In the CloudTrail console click Create trail to begin configuring a new trail.

configureTrail.title: Configure delivery, validation and CloudWatch integration
configureTrail.body: On the CloudTrail creation form set the following options:
items: Trail name and scope: enter a descriptive name; enable Apply trail to all accounts in my organization if you need org-wide collection.
S3 destination: choose Create new S3 bucket (or select an existing bucket) for raw log delivery.
Encryption: enable Log file SSE-KMS and select the appropriate KMS key.
Log file validation: enable to ensure integrity of delivered logs (recommended).
CloudWatch Logs: enable delivery to CloudWatch, select Use existing log group and enter the exact name utmstack.
IAM role: provide or create the role CloudTrail will assume to write to S3 and publish to CloudWatch.

eventTypes.title: Select event types
eventTypes.body: Enable the event categories required for monitoring and auditing.

management.label: 1 · Management events
management.body: Enable Management events and select All to record all API activity that manages AWS resources (create, update, delete).

data.label: 2 · Data events
data.body: Add a Data event. Choose S3 and select Log all events to capture object-level operations such as GetObject and PutObject.

network.label: 3 · Network activity events
network.body: In the Network Activities section add at least one service (e.g. ec2.amazonaws.com) and enable Log all events.

review.title: Review and create the trail
review.body: On the Configure event aggregation screen accept the defaults (or adjust if required). Review all settings and click Create trail.

intro.title: How it works
intro.body: UTMStack reads detections and audit activity directly from the CrowdStrike Falcon Event Streams API. You create an API client in Falcon with Event Streams scope; UTMStack runs an internal puller that streams events using those credentials. Nothing is installed on your endpoints or in Falcon.
intro.note: No agent is deployed by UTMStack — it pulls events from Falcon using the read-only API client credentials you provide below.

apiClients.title: Open API Clients and Keys
apiClients.body: In the Falcon console, open the menu (hamburger icon, top-left) and go to Support and resources → API Clients and Keys.

createClient.title: Create a new API client
createClient.body: Click Create API Client to start a new client definition.

scopes.title: Name the client and grant Event Streams scope
scopes.body: Give the client a descriptive name (UTMStack uses it to identify the event source) and select the API scopes required for Event Streams. Click Create to generate the credentials.

recordCredentials.title: Record the credentials
recordCredentials.body: Copy the Client ID, Client Secret and the Base URL for your CrowdStrike region. The secret is shown only once — store it securely. You will paste all three into the form below.

credentials.title: API client configuration
credentials.body: Use the credentials from the steps above to configure UTMStack. You can add more than one CrowdStrike client by saving additional configurations.

intro.title: How it works
intro.body: A custom integration ingests logs from any source the built-in modules do not cover. You install the UTMStack Forwarder, register a listener for your data with the protocol of your choice, and point your source at it.
intro.note: Pick the protocol your source can send (syslog UDP/TCP/TLS, or HTTP/HTTPS for JSON) below — the Forwarder creates the data type automatically.

choose.title: Choose protocol and port
choose.body: Select how your source sends data and the port the Forwarder should listen on, then run the activation command on the Forwarder host.
choose.tlsFirst: First load your TLS certificate and key on the Forwarder:
choose.authNote: To require authentication, append --auth bearer (token) or --auth hmac — the Forwarder prints a token to use in the Authorization header.

send.title: Point your source at the Forwarder
send.bodyNetwork: Configure your source to send <hl>{{proto}}</hl> syslog to <hl>{{host}}:{{port}}</hl>. Most devices have a remote-syslog or log-forwarding setting for this.
send.bodyHttp: Send your events as JSON via HTTP POST to <hl>{{endpoint}}</hl>. Each request body is one JSON event:
send.httpBindNote: The HTTP/HTTPS listener binds to 127.0.0.1 (the Forwarder host) by default, so post from an app running on that host — or front it with a reverse proxy. For remote sources, use syslog (UDP/TCP/TLS).

custom.parserBody: Incoming events are stored under the {{dataType}} data type. Add a parsing filter for it so the raw payload is mapped into structured fields, then build alert rules on top.

manualCommand.title: Optional — Enable via the command line instead
manualCommand.intro: Prefer the terminal? SSH into the Forwarder host and run the command below — it matches whatever protocol and port you have selected above.

remoteEnable.title: Enable this integration remotely
remoteEnable.body: Pick a Forwarder, choose the protocol and port, then enable the integration — no SSH needed.

modules.ESET: Ingest ESET PROTECT endpoint detections and telemetry to correlate multilayered malware defense across your estate.
modules.BITDEFENDER: Ingest Bitdefender GravityZone detections and endpoint telemetry to correlate threats across business devices.
modules.SENTINEL_ONE: Ingest SentinelOne endpoint detections and behavioral telemetry to correlate and investigate threats at scale.
modules.SOPHOS: Ingest Sophos Central detections across endpoint, server, firewall and email to correlate threats in one place.
modules.CROWDSTRIKE: Ingest CrowdStrike Falcon endpoint and workload detections to correlate cloud-native threat activity in UTMStack.
modules.CISCO: Ingest Cisco ASA firewall traffic, VPN and threat logs to monitor perimeter security and access within UTMStack.
modules.MERAKI: Ingest Cisco Meraki firewall and security-appliance syslog to monitor cloud-managed network traffic and threats.
modules.FIRE_POWER: Ingest Cisco Firepower NGFW and IPS logs to monitor intrusion attempts and threat activity at the perimeter.
modules.CISCO_SWITCH: Ingest Cisco switch syslog and telemetry to monitor network performance, configuration changes and security.
modules.FORTIGATE: Ingest Fortinet FortiGate NGFW traffic and threat logs to monitor perimeter security and network activity.
modules.FORTIWEB: Ingest Fortinet FortiWeb WAF logs to monitor web-application attacks and protect exposed services and APIs.
modules.SOPHOS_XG: Ingest Sophos XG firewall logs covering web filtering, IPS and VPN to monitor network traffic and threats.
modules.PALO_ALTO: Ingest Palo Alto Networks NGFW traffic and threat logs to monitor application usage and perimeter security.
modules.SONIC_WALL: Ingest SonicWall NGFW traffic and threat logs to monitor perimeter security and network activity in UTMStack.
modules.PFSENSE: Ingest pfSense firewall and router logs with unified threat management to monitor network traffic and threats.
modules.MIKROTIK: Ingest MikroTik RouterOS firewall, routing and wireless logs to monitor network activity and configuration.
modules.AIX: Collect IBM AIX Unix system, security and audit logs to monitor activity on IBM Power platforms within UTMStack.
modules.AS_400: Collect IBM AS/400 (IBM i) system and audit journals to monitor user activity on midrange OS/400 platforms.
modules.ORACLE: Ingest Oracle Database audit logs to monitor queries, access and privileged activity across your databases.
modules.SURICATA: Ingest Suricata IDS/IPS alerts and network events to detect intrusions and malicious traffic across the network.
modules.DECEPTIVE_BYTES: Ingest Deceptive Bytes alerts from its active endpoint-deception platform to surface attacker activity early.
modules.GITHUB: Ingest GitHub audit logs to monitor repository access, code changes and organization activity for source security.
modules.UTMSTACK: Ingest UTMStack's own SIEM and XDR telemetry to monitor platform health, internal activity and self-audit events.

FULL.name: Full access
FULL.desc: The operator can act inside your tenant as an administrator: change configuration, users and response flows.

supportAccess.fullWarning: Full access lets the operator change things on your behalf. Grant it while you need hands-on help, and drop back afterwards.
supportAccess.revokeNote: Everything the operator does here is recorded in your audit log.

toast.forbidden: Only an administrator of this tenant can change this

supportSession.full: full access — changes here are real
